description: Unified gene-program/cell-state model for the human liver, covering parenchymal cells (hepatocytes across the portal-to-central zonation axis, cholangiocytes), non-parenchymal stromal/vascular cells (hepatic stellate cells, sinusoidal/lymphatic/central-vein/vascular endothelial cells, Schwann cells ensheathing portal-tract nerves), and resident/infiltrating immune populations (B cells including plasma cells, T cells, myeloid cells including Kupffer cells and lipid-associated macrophages, NK cells, and mast cells). Each gene program lists up to 15 representative genes.

programs.name: Periportal (zone 1) metabolism
programs.function: Oxidative energy metabolism, gluconeogenesis, and ureagenesis enriched near the portal triad, where oxygen and nutrient tension are highest

programs.name: Pericentral (zone 3) metabolism
programs.function: Glycolysis, lipogenesis, and glutamine synthesis driven by the Wnt/beta-catenin gradient emanating from the central vein

programs.name: Bile acid synthesis and secretion
programs.function: Rate-limiting bile acid synthesis and canalicular bile acid transport

programs.name: Xenobiotic and drug metabolism
programs.function: Cytochrome P450-mediated phase I/II drug and toxin metabolism, concentrated pericentrally

programs.name: Lipid handling and lipoprotein assembly
programs.function: Fatty acid synthesis and VLDL/lipoprotein assembly and secretion

programs.name: Plasma protein and coagulation factor synthesis
programs.function: Synthesis and secretion of albumin, clotting factors, and acute-phase proteins

programs.name: Proliferation / regeneration
programs.function: Compensatory hepatocyte proliferation after injury or resection

programs.name: Lipid droplet accumulation (steatosis)
programs.function: Ectopic triglyceride storage characteristic of fatty liver disease

programs.name: Hepatocellular injury/stress response
programs.function: Stress-hormone and damage-response signaling following hepatotoxic or viral injury

programs.name: ER protein folding
programs.function: Folding of the very high secretory protein load produced by hepatocytes

programs.name: Interferon response
programs.function: Antiviral interferon-stimulated gene induction relevant to viral hepatitis

states.name: Peri-portal hepatocyte
states.phenotype: Zone 1 hepatocyte nearest the portal triad; oxygen- and nutrient-rich environment favoring oxidative and biosynthetic metabolism
states.notes: Classic zone-1 urea cycle / gluconeogenesis genes; ASS1, CPS1, ASL, ARG1, OTC, PCK1, G6PC, HAL, SDS are canonical periportal landmark genes in the Halpern et al. 2017 Nature single-cell spatial reconstruction of mouse liver zonation.

states.name: Mid-lobular hepatocyte
states.phenotype: Zone 2 hepatocyte occupying the transitional region between the portal triad and central vein, with a blended metabolic profile
states.notes: Evidence is genuinely thin: zone 2 has no widely validated unique marker set, and most literature (e.g. the 2021 Frontiers zonation review, Halpern 2017) describes it as a transcriptional gradient/blend between zone 1 and zone 3 rather than a discrete state. IGFBP2 is the one gene reported as relatively enriched in midlobular hepatocytes (2022 bioRxiv 'IGFBP2-expressing midlobular hepatocytes' study on regeneration); the remaining genes are pan-hepatocyte identity genes included because they are expressed at intermediate levels across the lobule, not because they are zone-2-specific. Fewer than 10 genes reflects this thin state-specific evidence rather than an oversight.

states.name: Central-lobular hepatocyte
states.phenotype: Zone 3 hepatocyte nearest the central vein; relatively hypoxic environment favoring glycolysis, lipogenesis, and xenobiotic detoxification, and most vulnerable to toxic/hypoxic injury
states.notes: GLUL, CYP2E1, CYP1A2, CYP3A4, OAT and RHBG are canonical zone-3/pericentral landmark genes from Halpern et al. 2017 (Nature) zonation atlas. AXIN2, LGR5, RNF43 and TBX3 mark the Wnt/RSPO3-responsive pericentral hepatocyte population described in Wang et al. 2015 (Nature, Axin2+ self-renewing pericentral hepatocytes) and Planas-Paz et al. 2016 (Nat Cell Biol, Wnt-RSPO3 axis controls zonation via TBX3).

states.name: Steatotic hepatocyte
states.phenotype: Lipid-laden hepatocyte characteristic of non-alcoholic/metabolic-associated fatty liver disease, typically emerging first in the pericentral zone
states.notes: Lipid-droplet coating proteins (PLIN2/PLIN5/CIDEA/CIDEC), lipogenic/uptake genes (CD36, DGAT2, SCD, SREBF1, MOGAT1, FABP1, PPARG) and the two major NAFLD/NASH genetic-risk genes PNPLA3 (Romeo et al., Nat Genet 2008) and TM6SF2 (Kozlitina et al., Nat Genet 2014) are well established steatotic hepatocyte markers.

states.name: Inflamed/injured hepatocyte
states.phenotype: Interferon-stimulated, stressed hepatocyte state seen in viral hepatitis and drug-induced liver injury
states.notes: Interferon-stimulated genes (ISG15, MX1, OAS1, IFIT1, IFIT3, STAT1, IRF1) are induced in hepatocytes during viral hepatitis (HBV/HCV) as part of the intrahepatic innate antiviral response; GDF15 and FGF21 are integrated-stress-response hepatokines induced by hepatocellular injury/DILI, and CDKN1A, ATF3, EGR1, HMGB1 mark acute hepatocyte stress/damage response.

programs.name: Cholangiocyte identity
programs.function: Mature bile duct epithelial transcriptional identity

programs.name: Bile fluid and bicarbonate modification
programs.function: CFTR/secretin-driven modification of bile fluid composition

programs.name: Mucin secretion
programs.function: Protective mucus layer lining the bile duct lumen

programs.name: Ductular reaction
programs.function: Reactive cholangiocyte proliferation and expansion seen in cholestasis and biliary injury

programs.name: Fibrogenic/inflammatory signaling
programs.function: Peribiliary inflammatory and fibrogenic signaling driving periductal fibrosis

states.name: Mature functional cholangiocyte
states.phenotype: Canonical healthy bile duct epithelial cell modifying bile composition
states.notes: Canonical mature biliary epithelial identity and bile-modification genes (CFTR, AQP1, SLC4A2) consistent with the Aizarani et al. 2019 (Nature) human liver cell atlas cholangiocyte cluster definitions.

states.name: Reactive cholangiocyte (ductular reaction)
states.phenotype: Proliferative, activated cholangiocyte state seen in primary sclerosing cholangitis, primary biliary cholangitis, and other cholestatic injury
states.notes: NCAM1 marks the reactive/neuroendocrine phenotype of ductular-reaction cholangiocytes in PSC and biliary atresia (Guicciardi et al., Hepatology 2020, 'Spectrum of Reactive Cholangiocytes in PSC'); SPP1 (osteopontin) is a well-documented mediator of biliary inflammation/fibrosis secreted by reactive cholangiocytes; ITGB6 is induced specifically in adaptive/reactive cholangiocyte populations surrounding the fibro-obliterative ductular reaction (bile-acid-activated macrophage/integrin avb6 literature).

states.name: Cholestatic cholangiocyte
states.phenotype: Impaired bile flow and bile-acid-induced toxicity characteristic of obstructive or autoimmune cholestasis
states.notes: Bile-acid/bicarbonate transport genes altered under cholestasis; ABCC3 (MRP3) is a classic compensatory basolateral bile-acid transporter upregulated in cholestatic liver disease; NR1H4 (FXR) is the bile-acid-sensing nuclear receptor central to cholestatic feedback; CLDN1 was recently shown to be a mediator/therapeutic target in PSC (2025 J Hepatol). Evidence here is more general cholangiocyte/cholestasis biology rather than a scRNA-seq-defined discrete cluster.

states.name: Cholangiocarcinoma-like cholangiocyte
states.phenotype: Neoplastic transformation driven by IDH1 mutation or FGFR2 fusion, precursor/tumor cell state of cholangiocarcinoma
states.notes: Driver mutation genes (IDH1, FGFR2 fusions, KRAS, TP53, ARID1A, BAP1, SMAD4, ERBB2, CDKN2A, PBRM1) reflect the established intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma genomic landscape (e.g. Farshidfar et al., Cell Reports 2017, IDH-mutant molecular subtype). S100P and SPP1 were identified as subtype markers distinguishing the two molecularly distinct iCCA subtypes (perihilar large-duct vs peripheral small-duct) in a single-cell RNA-seq study (Nat Commun 2022, 'two molecularly distinct subtypes of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma'). MUC5AC is part of a validated serum biomarker panel for CCA diagnosis. SOX9 marks biliary/cancer-stem-like differentiation in CCA.

programs.name: Pan-endothelial identity
programs.function: Baseline vascular-endothelial transcriptional identity shared across hepatic endothelial subtypes

programs.name: Liver sinusoidal endothelial identity and fenestration
programs.function: Specialized fenestrated, low-basement-membrane phenotype enabling hepatic macromolecule exchange between blood and hepatocytes

programs.name: Scavenger receptor-mediated endocytosis
programs.function: Clearance of hyaluronic acid, advanced glycation end-products, and other blood-borne macromolecules

programs.name: Continuous (vascular) endothelial identity
programs.function: Portal vein/hepatic artery continuous endothelium with basement membrane, distinct from fenestrated sinusoidal endothelium

programs.name: Central vein endothelial identity
programs.function: Wnt-ligand-producing central vein endothelium that establishes the pericentral hepatocyte zonation gradient

programs.name: Lymphatic endothelial identity
programs.function: PROX1-driven lymphatic endothelial program draining hepatic interstitial fluid

programs.name: Leukocyte adhesion
programs.function: Adhesion molecule upregulation enabling immune-cell trafficking into the liver

programs.name: Sinusoidal capillarization
programs.function: Loss of fenestrae and gain of basement membrane, converting sinusoidal endothelium toward a capillary-like phenotype in chronic liver disease and fibrosis

states.name: Sinusoidal endothelial cell
states.phenotype: Fenestrated, scavenger-receptor-high liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) lining hepatic sinusoids
states.notes: Canonical human/mouse LSEC identity and scavenger-receptor genes from Halpern et al. 2018 (Nat Biotechnol, paired-cell sequencing of liver endothelium), MacParland et al. 2018 (Nat Commun human liver atlas) and Aizarani et al. 2019 (Nature); OIT3 is highlighted as a robust LSEC-restricted hallmark gene (Nat. Signal Transduct Target Ther 2023).

states.name: Lymphatic endothelial cell
states.phenotype: PROX1+/PDPN+ lymphatic vessel endothelium draining hepatic interstitial fluid via portal tract lymphatics
states.notes: PROX1, PDPN(D2-40), FLT4(VEGFR3), LYVE1, CCL21 and MMRN1 are the standard pan-organ lymphatic endothelial identity panel; NRP2, SOX18 and FOXC2 are additional well-established lymphatic transcriptional regulators/markers from general vascular biology (not liver-specific), added because liver-specific lymphatic endothelial transcriptomic studies are limited (see Yamauchi et al. lymphatic marker podoplanin/D2-40 in cirrhotic liver).

states.name: Central vein endothelial cell
states.phenotype: Wnt-ligand-secreting endothelium of the central vein that establishes pericentral hepatocyte zonation
states.notes: WNT2, WNT9B and RSPO3 are the defining central-vein endothelial ligands that establish pericentral hepatocyte zonation (Wang et al. 2015 Nature; Planas-Paz et al. 2016 Nat Cell Biol; Halpern et al. 2018 Nat Biotechnol). KIT was specifically reported as abundant in central-vein-proximal liver endothelial cells and low/absent periportally (Halpern et al. 2018). PECAM1/CDH5/VWF/CD34 are generic pan-endothelial genes added to reach panel size since central-vein-specific literature is otherwise narrow; this is noted as comparatively thin state-specific evidence beyond the four Wnt-pathway genes.

states.name: Vascular endothelial cell
states.phenotype: Continuous, basement-membrane-bearing endothelium of the portal vein and hepatic artery, distinct from fenestrated sinusoidal endothelium
states.notes: EFNB2, DLL4 and LTBP4 mark periportal/portal-vein and hepatic-artery continuous (non-fenestrated) liver endothelium as distinct from sinusoidal LSECs (Halpern et al. 2018, Nat Biotechnol paired-cell sequencing); SOX17, HEY1, NOTCH4, BMX and GJA5 are established arterial/continuous-endothelium identity genes from general vascular biology used here to characterize the non-sinusoidal hepatic vasculature.

states.name: Capillarized (activated) sinusoidal endothelial cell
states.phenotype: Defenestrated, basement-membrane-gaining LSEC phenotype characteristic of liver fibrosis and cirrhosis
states.notes: Capillarization is defined by acquisition of a continuous-endothelium/basement-membrane phenotype: increased CD31/CD34/VWF with concurrent loss of fenestrae and gain of basement membrane genes (COL4A1, COL4A2, LAMB1, LAMA4, SPARC, FN1) (multiple LSEC defenestration/cirrhosis studies; CD34 reported as the more specific capillarization marker vs CD31). ACKR1+ and PLVAP+ endothelial cells were specifically shown by Ramachandran et al. 2019 (Nature, 'Resolving the fibrotic niche of human liver cirrhosis at single-cell level') to expand in cirrhosis and localize to the fibrotic niche, making them strong state-specific markers.

programs.name: Vitamin A / retinoid storage
programs.function: Cytoplasmic lipid droplets storing retinyl esters, hallmark of the quiescent state

programs.name: Myofibroblast activation
programs.function: Trans-differentiation into a proliferative, contractile myofibroblast-like phenotype

programs.name: Extracellular matrix production
programs.function: Collagen and fibronectin deposition driving liver fibrosis

programs.name: Contractile / portal pressure regulation
programs.function: Endothelin-driven sinusoidal contraction contributing to portal blood flow resistance and portal hypertension

programs.name: Apoptosis
programs.function: Programmed cell death; a mechanism of fibrosis resolution

states.name: Quiescent HSC
states.phenotype: Vitamin A-storing, non-proliferative resting perisinusoidal cell in the healthy liver
states.notes: Canonical quiescent HSC identity and vitamin-A storage genes as reviewed in Tsuchida & Friedman 2017 (Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol, 'Mechanisms of hepatic stellate cell activation'); LRAT and RBP1 are specifically required for retinyl-ester storage in quiescent HSC lipid droplets.

states.name: Activated HSC
states.phenotype: Myofibroblast-like fibrogenic activation driving liver fibrosis in chronic injury (viral hepatitis, NASH, alcohol-related liver disease)
states.notes: Standard myofibroblast transdifferentiation panel (alpha-SMA/ACTA2, TAGLN, CNN1, MYH11, PDGFRB/PDGFRA, TGF-beta/SMAD signaling, early collagen induction) per Tsuchida & Friedman 2017 review and Mederacke et al. 2013 (Nat Commun, HSC lineage tracing as origin of myofibroblasts).

states.name: Fibrotic (end-stage) HSC
states.phenotype: Sustained ECM deposition characteristic of advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis
states.notes: This state had zero genes previously. Sustained ECM deposition genes (COL1A1/COL1A2/COL3A1, TIMP1, PDGFRA) mark the scar-associated myofibroblast population defined by Ramachandran et al. 2019 (Nature, 'Resolving the fibrotic niche of human liver cirrhosis'); LOXL2 (collagen crosslinking) and TNC/POSTN/THBS2 (matricellular ECM genes enriched in the fibrotic niche) are drawn from Dobie et al. 2019 (Cell Reports, 'Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers zonation of function in the mesenchyme during liver fibrosis'). Note: transcriptionally, 'end-stage fibrotic' HSC/myofibroblasts overlap substantially with 'activated' HSC in current single-cell literature; a fully distinct end-stage-specific signature (vs. simply higher magnitude/duration of the activation program) is not yet crisply established, so some overlap with the activated-hsc panel is expected and appropriate.

states.name: Reverting (inactivating) HSC
states.phenotype: Partial return toward quiescence during fibrosis regression after removal of the injurious stimulus
states.notes: This state had zero genes previously. Evidence is genuinely limited: Kisseleva et al. 2012 (PNAS, 'Myofibroblasts revert to an inactive phenotype during regression of liver fibrosis') and Troeger et al. 2012 (Gastroenterology, 'Deactivation of hepatic stellate cells during liver fibrosis resolution in mice') show that a fraction of activated HSC/myofibroblasts partially re-express quiescence-associated genes (RGS5, HGF, NGFR, DES, GFAP) and PPARG (adipogenic/quiescence transcription factor) while down-regulating but not fully losing activation markers (PDGFRB, VIM retained at intermediate levels), and that these 'inactivated' cells remain primed to reactivate faster upon re-injury. A precise, validated 'reverting-specific' gene signature distinct from quiescent HSC has not been firmly established in the literature, so this panel is intentionally kept under 10 genes and should be treated as lower-confidence than the other three HSC states.

programs.name: Antibody (immunoglobulin) secretion
programs.function: Plasma-cell differentiation and immunoglobulin production, including anti-mitochondrial antibody production in primary biliary cholangitis

states.name: Naive B cell
states.phenotype: Circulating antigen-inexperienced B cell
states.notes: Core B-lineage identity (CD19/MS4A1/CD79A/CD79B/PAX5/BANK1/CD22) plus markers specific to the naive (antigen-inexperienced) subset: co-expression of unswitched IGHD/IGHM, TCL1A (highly and preferentially expressed in naive/transitional B cells), FCER2/CD23 and IL4R (naive/quiescence markers), and CCR7/SELL which mark recirculating naive lymphocytes not yet retained in tissue.

states.name: Activated B cell
states.phenotype: Antigen-engaged, proliferating B cell
states.notes: Classic B-cell activation markers upregulated upon antigen/BCR engagement and CD40 signaling (CD69, CD86, CD80, CD40, CD83, FAS/CD95), proliferation genes (MYC, MKI67, CCND2), AICDA (activation-induced deaminase, induced upon activation for SHM/CSR), early IRF4 induction preceding terminal plasma-cell commitment, and TNFRSF13B (TACI) upregulation with activation.

states.name: Plasma cell
states.phenotype: Terminally differentiated antibody-secreting B cell, expanded in autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis
states.notes: Canonical terminally-differentiated antibody-secreting cell program: master transcription factors PRDM1(BLIMP1)/IRF4/XBP1, surface markers SDC1(CD138) and CD38, secretory-pathway/UPR genes supporting high immunoglobulin output (JCHAIN, MZB1, SSR4, DERL3, FKBP11), immunoglobulin isotype transcripts (IGHG1/IGHA1), and TNFRSF17 (BCMA), a well-established long-lived plasma cell survival receptor.

states.name: Memory B cell
states.phenotype: Long-lived antigen-experienced B cell poised for rapid recall response
states.notes: CD27 is the most widely used human memory B-cell marker but is explicitly not universal (a CD27-negative memory subset exists; noted in recent literature). Panel combines CD27 with other markers reported as enriched on memory versus naive B cells (high CD80, TNFRSF13B/TACI, CD44, FAS/CD95, CR2/CD21, CD24) and recirculation/homing receptors (CXCR4, S1PR1, ITGB1, CCR6). Confidence is slightly lower here than for the other B-cell states because no single marker set is universally agreed upon for human memory B cells.

programs.name: Tissue-resident memory program
programs.function: CD69/CXCR6-driven retention program of liver-resident memory T cells

programs.name: Exhaustion program
programs.function: Chronic-stimulation-induced dysfunction limiting cytotoxic output, prominent in chronic HBV/HCV infection

states.name: Naive/circulating T cell
states.phenotype: Circulating, antigen-inexperienced T cell not yet retained in the liver
states.notes: Standard naive/circulating T-cell signature: lymph-node homing receptors CCR7 and SELL (CD62L), transcription factors TCF7 and LEF1 that define stemness/naivety, costimulatory receptors CD27/CD28 retained from thymic egress, core TCR-complex genes (CD3D, CD3E, TRAC) for T-lineage identity, IL7R for naive T-cell survival, and S1PR1/KLF2 which govern egress and recirculation (and are downregulated upon tissue residency, providing contrast with the Trm state).

states.name: Tissue-resident memory T cell (Trm)
states.phenotype: CD69+CXCR6+ liver-resident memory T cell retained in the hepatic sinusoids, poised for rapid recall response
states.notes: Reflects the well-characterized human liver Trm core signature (Pallett et al., Sci Rep 2017; Kumar et al., Cell Rep 2017): CD69 and ITGAE (CD103) as canonical residency markers, CXCR6 which is highly enriched on CD69+ intrahepatic CD8+ T cells (~90%) versus blood, ITGA1 (CD49a) and RGS1 as part of the core Trm adhesion/retention signature, and the transcription factors ZNF683 (Hobit), RUNX3 and PRDM1 that cooperatively drive tissue-resident memory differentiation. CXCR3 supports liver homing. Human hepatic Trm notably also express CD103 (ITGAE), distinguishing them from mouse Trm.

states.name: Cytotoxic activated T cell
states.phenotype: Effector CD8+ state driving hepatocyte killing in viral hepatitis and autoimmune hepatitis
states.notes: Standard effector CD8+ cytotoxic program: cytolytic granule components (GZMB, GZMA, GZMK, PRF1, NKG7), death-receptor ligand FASLG, effector cytokines (IFNG, TNF, IL2), the master effector transcription factors TBX21 (T-bet) and EOMES, KLRG1 as a terminal-effector marker, and CD8A confirming the CD8 lineage; this program is directly implicated in hepatocyte killing in viral and autoimmune hepatitis.

states.name: Exhausted T cell
states.phenotype: Dysfunctional state arising from chronic antigen exposure in chronic HBV/HCV infection and hepatocellular carcinoma
states.notes: Panel reflects the widely-replicated chronic-antigen/exhaustion signature seen in chronic HBV/HCV and HCC studies: co-inhibitory receptors (PDCD1, LAG3, HAVCR2/TIM-3, TIGIT, CD160, BTLA, CTLA4), the exhaustion master transcription factor TOX, markers of terminal exhaustion (ENTPD1/CD39, CD38, LAYN), the CXCL13 chemokine signature associated with dysfunctional/exhausted intratumoral and intrahepatic T cells, and TNFRSF9 (4-1BB) marking chronically antigen-engaged exhausted cells.

states.name: Regulatory T cell
states.phenotype: Tolerogenic Treg state restraining autoimmune attack on hepatocytes and bile ducts
states.notes: Canonical Treg identity/suppressive program: master transcription factor FOXP3, IL2RA (CD25) and IKZF2 (Helios), co-inhibitory/costimulatory receptors CTLA4, TNFRSF18 (GITR), TNFRSF4 (OX40); the ectoenzyme pair ENTPD1 (CD39)/NT5E (CD73) mediating adenosine-based suppression, which is specifically reported as upregulated on intrahepatic Tregs; TGFB1 and IL10 as suppressive cytokines; and TIGIT, which is highly enriched on and functionally important for intrahepatic Tregs in chronic liver disease.

programs.name: Phagocytosis and antigen processing
programs.function: Efferocytosis, clearance of gut-derived bacteria/endotoxin, and aged red blood cell removal

programs.name: M2 reparative/alternative polarization
programs.function: Alternatively activated, tissue-remodeling and anti-inflammatory program

programs.name: Lipid handling (lipid-associated macrophage) program
programs.function: TREM2/CD9-driven lipid uptake and handling in the fibrotic/steatotic niche

programs.name: Monocyte recruitment / infiltration
programs.function: Chemokine-receptor-driven recruitment of circulating monocytes into the liver

programs.name: Matrix remodeling
programs.function: Matrix metalloproteinase-driven ECM turnover around fibrotic septa

states.name: Kupffer cell
states.phenotype: Liver-resident, self-renewing macrophage lining hepatic sinusoids that clears gut-derived bacteria/endotoxin and aged red blood cells
states.notes: Core Kupffer-cell identity/self-renewal signature converged upon by human and mouse liver macrophage atlases (MARCO, VSIG4, CD5L, TIMD4, CLEC4F, FOLR2, CD163, VCAM1) plus the transcription factors ID3 and SPIC that specify Kupffer-cell fate, and HMOX1/SLC40A1 reflecting the iron/erythrophagocytosis handling niche function. CLEC4F is the most specific single marker in mouse; MARCO/VSIG4/CD5L/TIMD4/FOLR2/CD163 are the best cross-species human markers.

states.name: Lipid-associated macrophage (LAM)
states.phenotype: TREM2+CD9+ scar/lipid-associated macrophage expanding around fibrotic septa and steatotic hepatocytes in NASH
states.notes: Directly matches the TREM2+CD9+ 'scar-associated macrophage' (SAM) population defined by Ramachandran et al. 2019 Nature in human cirrhotic liver, which co-expresses GPNMB, SPP1, FABP5 and CD63, and the convergent TREM2+ lipid-associated macrophage (LAM) signature from NASH/MASH liver atlases (APOE, APOC1, LPL, LGALS3, cathepsins CTSD/CTSB/CTSK reflecting the osteoclast-like lipid-handling program).

states.name: Monocyte-derived inflammatory macrophage
states.phenotype: Recruited monocyte-derived macrophage driving acute inflammation in hepatitis and acute liver injury
states.notes: CD14+ classical monocyte-derived infiltrate signature (S100A8, S100A9, VCAN, FCN1, CD14) used to distinguish recirculating inflammatory macrophages from resident Kupffer cells in acute-on-chronic liver failure and viral-hepatitis scRNA-seq studies, combined with the CCR2/CCL2 recruitment axis and M1 pro-inflammatory effectors (TNF, IL1B, IL6, CXCL10, PTGS2).

states.name: Restorative/reparative macrophage
states.phenotype: Anti-inflammatory, tissue-repair-promoting macrophage supporting resolution of injury
states.notes: Based on Ramachandran/Iredale et al. 2012 PNAS (PMID 23100531), which defined the Ly6C(lo) 'restorative' macrophage subset in resolving liver fibrosis: this population is the principal MMP-expressing subset (MMP9, MMP12, MMP13), upregulates IGF1 and GPNMB, and acquires an anti-inflammatory/efferocytic phenotype (MERTK-GAS6 axis, high phagocytic MRC1/CD163/STAB1, IL10/TGFB1). Direct human single-cell evidence for this exact state is sparser than for Kupffer cells or LAMs — this list leans on the mouse fibrosis-resolution literature translated to human orthologs, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

programs.name: Activating/inhibitory receptor signaling
programs.function: Integration of activating and inhibitory NK receptor signals

programs.name: Liver-residency program
programs.function: CXCR6/CD49a-driven retention program of liver-resident NK cells (ILC1-like)

programs.name: Exhaustion/dysfunction program
programs.function: Reduced cytotoxic function characteristic of chronic HCV infection and hepatocellular carcinoma

states.name: Circulating (conventional) NK cell
states.phenotype: CD56dim/CD16+ conventional cytotoxic NK cell recruited from blood
states.notes: Canonical CD56dim/CD16+ (FCGR3A+) peripheral-blood-derived NK signature. CX3CR1 and S1PR5 mark blood/circulating egress-competent NK cells and are specifically reported as absent from liver-resident CD56bright NK cells, providing the key discriminator from the liver-resident state. SPON2 and FGFBP2 are established CD56dim-selective transcriptomic markers from NK scRNA-seq atlases. Fewer liver-specific papers directly profile this 'default' circulating subset since most liver NK literature focuses on contrasting it against resident populations.

states.name: Liver-resident NK cell (ILC1-like)
states.phenotype: CXCR6+CD49a+ tissue-resident NK/ILC1 population uniquely enriched in liver sinusoids
states.notes: CXCR6+CD49a(ITGA1)+CD69+ tissue-residency signature from Stegmann et al. 2016 (CXCR6 marks T-bet(lo)Eomes(hi) liver NK), Hudspeth/Cuff et al. 2017 Sci Rep (Hobit/ZNF683 in CD56bright liver-resident NK), and Cell Reports 2022 liver-type ILC1 scRNA-seq (IL7R, AHR, LTB, CD160, KLRB1, CD9). Both TBX21 and EOMES are included because reported transcription-factor patterns differ across studies (Marquardt et al. report Tbet+Eomes+, Stegmann et al. report Tbet-lo/Eomes-hi), reflecting genuine heterogeneity between liver-resident NK and ILC1-like subsets rather than a single settled marker set.

states.name: Cytotoxic activated NK cell
states.phenotype: IFN-gamma/granzyme-high effector state engaged during viral hepatitis or anti-tumor immune surveillance
states.notes: Standard cytotoxic/effector NK activation signature (granzymes, perforin, IFN-gamma, Fas-ligand, TRAIL/TNFSF10, activating receptor NKG2D/KLRK1, proliferation marker MKI67) consistent with the hyper-activated/degranulating NK phenotype described during acute viral hepatitis and anti-tumor surveillance (Björkström, Marquardt liver NK studies). This is a general cytotoxic-effector program rather than a liver-exclusive one, but is well established in liver immunology contexts.

states.name: Exhausted/dysfunctional NK cell
states.phenotype: Reduced cytotoxic function and elevated inhibitory receptor expression characteristic of chronic HCV infection and hepatocellular carcinoma
states.notes: Inhibitory-receptor/exhaustion signature drawn from chronic HCV and HCC NK-dysfunction literature: HAVCR2 (TIM-3) and TIGIT co-expression marks exhausted NK in HBV/HCV-HCC (Oncoimmunology 2021); CD96 correlates with NK exhaustion and poor prognosis in HCC (Hepatology, Sun et al.); KLRC1 (NKG2A) is a defined NK exhaustion checkpoint for HCV persistence (Zhang et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30944315); CD244 (2B4) is upregulated on dysfunctional NK/T cells in chronic HCV. Only 10 genes are listed because impairment of activating receptors (KLRK1/NKG2D, NCR3/NKp30, KLRD1/CD94) is reported as reduced expression/function rather than a clean 'up' marker, so this list is somewhat heterogeneous in direction — evidence is real but less uniformly 'marker-like' than the other three NK states.

programs.name: Degranulation
programs.function: Release of preformed histamine and protease-containing granules

programs.name: Fibrogenic crosstalk
programs.function: Protease and cytokine signaling implicated in promoting hepatic-stellate-cell activation and periductal fibrosis around bile ducts

states.name: Resting mast cell
states.phenotype: Quiescent tissue-resident mast cell
states.notes: Standard tissue-resident mast-cell identity program, present regardless of activation state: KIT (CD117) and the master transcription factors GATA2/MITF that specify mast-cell lineage, granule protease genes (TPSAB1, TPSB2, CPA3, CMA1), the high-affinity IgE receptor components (MS4A2/FcER1beta, FCER1A), histamine biosynthesis/storage machinery (HDC, SLC18A2/VMAT2) reflecting a fully granule-loaded quiescent cell, and IL1RL1 (ST2), constitutively expressed on resting mast cells.

states.name: Degranulated/activated mast cell
states.phenotype: IgE-triggered or injury-triggered degranulation releasing histamine and proteases
states.notes: Combines the released-granule proteases (TPSAB1, CMA1) and histamine synthesis gene (HDC) with the canonical IgE/FcERI proximal signaling cascade that triggers degranulation (FCER1A, SYK, LYN, LAT, PLCG1), plus the de novo cytokine/chemokine response mounted after activation (IL6, TNF, CXCL8, IL13), well established in IgE-mediated mast-cell activation literature.

states.name: Fibrogenic mast cell
states.phenotype: Chronic activation state implicated in promoting periductal and parenchymal fibrosis via hepatic-stellate-cell crosstalk, notably around bile ducts in cholangiopathies
states.notes: Evidence for a discrete 'fibrogenic mast cell' transcriptional state is limited; this list is built from mechanistic studies showing mast-cell chymase (CMA1) and tryptase (TPSAB1) promote hepatic stellate cell activation/transdifferentiation and correlate with fibrosis stage, with TGFB1 as the principal profibrotic mediator secreted by activated mast cells, plus angiogenic/growth factors (VEGFA, FGF2) and cytokines (IL13, TNF) implicated in mast-cell-driven fibrogenesis in chronic liver disease. Kept below 10-15 genes deliberately given the thinner, largely indirect (not scRNA-seq-defined) evidence base; do not treat this as a validated single-cell signature.

states.name: Degranulation-exhausted mast cell
states.phenotype: Post-degranulation refractory state with depleted granule stores
states.notes: No validated transcriptional signature for a distinct post-degranulation 'exhausted/refractory' mast-cell state currently exists in the literature; a 2026 bioRxiv preprint on IgE-desensitized mast cells describes ~168 upregulated genes enriched for immunoregulatory pathways but does not name a canonical marker panel, and is not yet peer-reviewed. Genes listed here reflect degranulation-history/refractoriness proxies used in functional assays (CD63 as a degranulation marker, SYK as the desensitized/uncoupled signaling node, HDC/IL6 reflecting ongoing but blunted mediator regeneration) rather than an established exhaustion signature. Intentionally left short of 10 genes rather than padded; flag this state as the weakest-supported in the whole set.

programs.name: Schwann-cell identity
programs.function: Mature peripheral glial transcriptional identity ensheathing hepatic portal-tract nerves

programs.name: Myelination
programs.function: Formation and maintenance of the myelin sheath around large-caliber axons

programs.name: Non-myelinating (Remak) program
programs.function: Ensheathment of bundles of small unmyelinated autonomic fibers, the predominant Schwann-cell phenotype in hepatic portal-tract innervation

programs.name: Neurotrophic factor signaling
programs.function: Production of neurotrophic factors supporting nerve maintenance and regeneration

programs.name: Repair (dedifferentiation) program
programs.function: c-Jun-driven dedifferentiation into a proliferative, repair-supportive phenotype after nerve or tissue injury

states.name: Myelinating Schwann cell
states.phenotype: Ensheathes larger myelinated hepatic autonomic/sensory nerve fibers in the portal tract
states.notes: Canonical peripheral myelin gene program: structural myelin proteins (MPZ, PLP1, MBP, PMP22, MAG, PRX, CNP), the master myelination transcription factor EGR2 (KROX20), the pan-Schwann-lineage transcription factor SOX10 and marker S100B, GJB1 (connexin-32, mutated in CMT1X, myelinating-Schwann-specific gap junction protein), and CLDN19, part of the paranodal/myelin tight-junction machinery specific to myelinating Schwann cells.

states.name: Non-myelinating (Remak) Schwann cell
states.phenotype: Ensheathes bundles of small unmyelinated autonomic fibers, the predominant Schwann-cell type in hepatic portal-tract innervation
states.notes: Remak/non-myelinating program per Schwann-cell marker reviews (e.g., Harty & Monk, 'Unwrapping the unappreciated: recent progress in Remak Schwann cell biology'): retained immature-state markers NGFR (p75NTR), L1CAM, NCAM1, GAP43 and EGR1, GFRA3 (GDNF-family co-receptor associated with non-myelinating fibers/nociceptive axon association), and pan-Schwann genes SOX10/S100B/ERBB3/CDH19 shared with the myelinating lineage but retained alongside the immature marker set.

states.name: Repair (injury-activated) Schwann cell
states.phenotype: c-Jun-driven dedifferentiated, proliferative phenotype supporting nerve and tissue repair after hepatic injury
states.notes: Directly reflects the Jessen & Mirsky 'repair Schwann cell' model (J Physiol 2016): c-JUN as the master regulator of the repair phenotype, driving autocrine trophic factor expression (SHH, GDNF, NRG1, IGF1, TGFB1); re-expression of developmental/precursor transcription factors SOX2 and POU3F1 (Oct6); re-upregulation of premyelinating-state markers NGFR (p75NTR), GFAP, L1CAM and NCAM1 following loss of axonal contact; and RUNX2, recently reported to drive the repair-phenotype chromatin switch and SOX2 activation after nerve injury.
